To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

supply chain management is the integration of key business processes from end user through original supplier that provides products, services, and information that add value for customers and other stakeholders.
SCM is the management of upstream and downstream relationships with suppliers and customers to deliver superior customer value at less cost to the supply chain as a whole.

supply chain management is the integration of key business processes across the supply chain for the purpose of improving the long-term performance of the individual companies and the supply chain as a whole.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: What is SCM? What does it encompass? What are its boundaries? How does it differ from logistics? What is the relationship between logistics and SCM? How do we define SCM in a way that will be accepted by practitioners? What are the benefits to practitioners?
identifying the key issues and developing a framework for the study of SCM.
identifying and defining the elements and relationships that comprise a conceptual model for SCM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the SCM concept is an extension of logistics and that the SCM concept should be viewed as an all encompass ing business management approach that includes logistics, purchasing, marketing and other business functions.

SCM is the process of strategically managing the activities that procure raw materials, transform these materials into intermediate and finished products, and distribute the finished products to customers.
SCM is the integration of key business processes from end user through original suppliers that provides products, services, and information that add value for customers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
supply chain management is more than a new name for logistics, but rather a new approach to business integration.

supply chain management is the integration of key business processes from end-user through original-source supplier that provides products, services, and information that add value for customers and stakeholders.

SCM is a process that links the entire supply chain from raw material to end user, and that it includes all of the activities and processes required to move the product from raw material to final customer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the concept of SCM is not new, and it is not just logistics.
SCM is a process that involves the integration of business functions and business processes within and across organizations in order to achieve a competitive advantage in a supply chain.
SCM is a new and distinct concept that extends the traditional concept of logistics to include a broader set of activities, processes, and functions.
